Question: “神舟六号”飞船 from launch to return stages, mechanical energy conserved in which stage?
Options:
A. accelerating ascent stage
B. circular orbit around Earth stage
C. entering atmosphere deceleration stage
D. parachute open descent stage

Mechanical energy conservation when only gravity (conservative force) does work? For spacecraft:
A: rocket engines do positive work, mechanical energy increases, not conserved.
B: In circular orbit around Earth, if no atmospheric drag or thrust, only gravity acts. But gravity is central conservative, mechanical energy (kinetic + gravitational potential) constant for circular orbit. In high school physics, satellite in circular orbit under gravity mechanical energy conserved. Need check if gravitational potential considered? Yes. In circular orbit kinetic and potential constant, mechanical energy conserved. If there is residual atmosphere? Ideally no. B.
C: entering atmosphere, air resistance does negative work, mechanical energy decreases (converted to heat), not conserved.
D: parachute open, air resistance, not conserved.
Thus answer B.

Need maybe parse "机械能守恒" in high school: only gravity/elastic force work. In orbit gravity does work? In circular orbit gravity perpendicular to velocity, does no work, kinetic constant, potential constant, so mechanical energy constant. More generally in elliptical orbit mechanical energy conserved if only gravity. So B.
